title: Peter Cook (architect)
summary: This document is a biographical article about Sir Peter Cook, an English architect, lecturer, and writer, best known as a founder of the avant-garde architectural group Archigram. The article begins with an overview of his life, noting his 1936 birth, his knighthood in 2007, and his recognition through the Royal Gold Medal awarded to Archigram in 2004. It then details his early life and education in Essex and his architectural training at Bournemouth College of Art and the Architectural Association School of Architecture in London. The career section highlights his academic leadership roles, including directorship of the Institute of Contemporary Arts and chair of architecture at The Bartlett, as well as his notable built works such as the Kunsthaus Graz in Austria, the Vienna University of Economics and Business law faculty, the Abedian School of Architecture in Australia, and his UK buildings at Arts University Bournemouth, plus a 2025 Play Pavilion at Serpentine London created with LEGO. The document also includes a chronological list of his awards and honours (1960–2010), his successes in architectural competitions, his current academic appointments, his exhibition and curatorial activities, and an extensive bibliography of his publications spanning 1967 to 2026, concluding with references and external links to interviews and related resources.
